forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Cambridgeshire pension fund funding level falls to 132% despite strong investment returns
news_drafts.lead: The Cambridgeshire Pension Fund's formal actuarial valuation showed a funding level—the ratio of assets to liabilities—of 147% at 31 March 2025, but updated monitoring a year later revealed it had fallen to 132%. The drop occurred despite assets growing by £355.2 million to £5.26 billion and investment returns reaching 6.6%, which generated £378.1 million in gains. The fund's annual report attributes the decline to "movements in the Fund's assets and liabilities" but does not specify the cause. The shift suggests that pension liabilities grew faster than assets during the year, even as the fund achieved positive investment performance. The fund, which administered 102,596 pension records across 185 employers, maintained strong employer contribution collection with 99.6% of the £171.5 million in annual contributions received on time.

findings.committee: Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee
findings.headline: Mortuary service demand expected to continue increasing in line with demographic trends
findings.detail: In 2025, 2,765 deaths reported to Coroner with 1,204 requiring post-mortem examination. Demand expected to continue increasing. Contract structured on demand-led, per-case charging basis, meaning actual annual costs will vary with activity. Baseline £1.28m excludes future price uplifts, which will be considered annually at council discretion subject to available funding.
findings.matters: Rising demand creates budget pressure on a non-discretionary statutory service; actual annual costs could exceed baseline if demand continues to increase, requiring council to find additional funding through annual reviews
findings.figures: 2,765 deaths reported to the Coroner, of which 1,204 required a post-mortem examination in 2025; demand expected to continue to increase in line with demographic trends
findings.quote: Demand for the service has remained high and is expected to continue to increase in line with demographic trends and annual case volumes. The actual value of the arrangement will vary depending on activity levels.

findings.committee: Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee
findings.headline: Three-year mortuary services contract from April 2027 valued at approximately £1.28m over the term
findings.detail: Council proposing three-year contract with North West Anglia NHS Trust commencing April 1, 2027, following expiry of current arrangements on March 31, 2027. Contract includes option to extend for one further year. Estimated value £1.28m over initial three-year term, though actual cost will vary depending on activity levels and demand for the service.
findings.matters: Material multi-year financial commitment for statutory service requiring council budget planning; actual annual costs dependent on activity levels create budget uncertainty
findings.quote: The proposed arrangement has an assured value of approximately £1.28m over the initial three-year term. This value does not include any future annual price uplifts.

findings.headline: Planning overspend of £183k forecast linked to enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and Saxon Pit planning appeal costs
findings.detail: The planning budget is forecasting an overspend of £183k linked to an enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and anticipated costs arising from the Saxon Pit planning appeal. The position will continue to be monitored throughout the year.
findings.matters: Appeal costs are unpredictable and can escalate; this indicates where planning and enforcement decisions are creating unbudgeted financial obligations.
findings.quote: Planning: the planning budget is forecasting an overspend of £183k linked to an enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and anticipated costs arising from the Saxon Pit planning appeal.

findings.headline: Energy Projects overspend of £631k forecast, driven by higher operating costs and lower-than-expected St Ives Park & Ride revenue
findings.detail: Operating costs across all energy schemes are significantly higher than originally forecast, driven mainly by increased operation and maintenance contract costs, higher imported electricity charges and rising insurance premiums. The St Ives Park & Ride scheme is particularly affected, with lower-than-expected revenue generation due to limited EV charging take-up and delays in connecting a direct customer.
findings.matters: Schemes not performing operationally as projected indicate either forecasting weakness or genuine market challenges; the St Ives Park & Ride revenue shortfall is material for debt serviceability and the viability of council capital assumptions.
findings.quote: Energy Projects: an overspend of £631k is forecast. Operating costs across all energy schemes are significantly higher than originally forecast, driven mainly by increased operation and maintenance contract costs, higher imported electricity charges and rising insurance premiums.

findings.headline: Waste Management underspend of £1.3m has reduced from previous months owing to bulky waste volumes and Energy from Waste contract delays
findings.detail: The waste budget is forecasting an underspend of £1.3m driven by increased diversion of waste from landfill to Energy from Waste treatment and separate food waste collections. However, the underspend has declined from earlier forecasts due to increased volumes of bulky waste received and delays in agreeing an Energy from Waste offtake contract, though higher food waste capture rates may offset some of this impact.
findings.matters: Waste is a major controllable cost for councils; declining underspends indicate emerging pressures that could reverse expected savings and affect financial delivery assumptions.
findings.quote: this has reduced from the underspend forecast in previous months owing to increased volumes of bulky waste received and delays in agreeing an Energy from Waste offtake contract.
